From #209's interface study. The worktree pre-flight is the single widest-reaching hand procedure measured — **more agents run it than any other loop** — and it is the one whose failure destroys work.

## Why

Measured across all 214 session transcripts: **212 `Bash` calls doing `git worktree add|list|remove|prune` or `git status` as a pre-flight, across 106 of 214 agents.** Collapsing that to one call per session is worth **0.15–0.34% of the bill** at the measured 13,911 input-equivalents per agent turn, plus ~106 tokens off `CLAUDE.md`'s prefix (0.05%).

The correctness case is the real one and it is already on the record: #105 is open, worktree assignment handed two agents one tree **five times in one evening** (2026-08-02), and `CLAUDE.md`'s standing mitigation is a *prose* pre-flight — "verify it is exclusively yours — clean `git status`, and no foreign uncommitted files appearing during the run". The 212 calls show agents do run it. The five collisions show that a pre-flight an agent performs from memory, ad hoc, in whatever form it improvises, is not the same as one that always runs the same checks.

The user's own standing note on this project is blunt about it: never assume harness worktree isolation.

## What

`just worktree add <name>` — fetch, create, prove exclusivity, print what the agent needs, in one call:

1. `git fetch origin`
2. `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main --detach`
3. Pre-flight the result: clean `git status`, no foreign untracked files, no other live registration pointing at the same path
4. Print the absolute path and the base SHA — the two things every dispatch briefing then has to restate

and `just worktree list` for the hygiene sweep (85 live registrations are on record), plus `just worktree check` to re-run the pre-flight mid-run without creating anything.

Typed refusals, named and actionable:

| Refusal | When |
|---|---|
| `worktree_occupied` | the path already exists or is registered — **name the other holder** (registration, HEAD, whether its tree is dirty), because #105's damage came from not knowing |
| `dirty_tree` | uncommitted or foreign untracked files present |
| `stale_registration` | registered but the directory is gone — prune is the fix, and it should say so, not do it silently |

## Acceptance criteria

1. `just worktree add <name>` performs all four steps and refuses with a named class rather than a raw git error.
2. `worktree_occupied` prints the competing holder's metadata. A refusal that does not say who else is there repeats #105's actual failure.
3. **It never resets, cleans, or removes anything on the refusal path.** `CLAUDE.md` is explicit: foreign files mean stop and report, never reset. A recipe that tidies is a recipe that destroys work.
4. `just worktree check` runs the pre-flight alone, non-destructive, safe to run mid-task.
5. The ladder is Python under pytest per ADR-0049 (bash at the process seam only), with the refusal classification unit-tested in the no-Arma tier.
6. The closing comment quotes the before/after call count for one real dispatch.

## Scope

**This does not close #105.** Worktree *assignment* is the orchestrator's and stays there; this makes the pre-flight cheap, uniform and loud. Say so in the close and leave #105 open.

## The gated-row collision

`CLAUDE.md`'s command surface table is human-gated — propose the row in the close per ADR-0057's reconciliation clause, together with a proposed shortening of the working-style pre-flight bullet to a pointer at the recipe. Do not land either unilaterally.

## Gate

No Arma surface. `just fast`.

Refs #209, #195 (idea 3, loop L4), #105.
